instruction: I have received job application emails for Sales Manager role over the last 2 weeks. I need you to do two things for my ongoing recruiting process. 1. Create a "job_applications.csv" file with the headers "First Name", "Last Name" and "LinkedIn URL" fields, the values of which should be extracted from the emails. Skip ones who did not provide their LinkedIn URLs in their emails. 2. Download their email attachments in "attachments/<first_name>__<last_name>/" directory. Replace <first_name> and <last_name> as per their names (lower cased), and use file names as per their attachment names in the email. The csv file and "attachments/" directory should be in "~/documents/work/recruiting/" directory in my file system.
notes: Two apps (gmail, file_system) plus supervisor. The inbox is searched with query 'Sales Manager' and min_created_at two weeks before the current date; each matching thread is read with show_thread, which reveals the applicant's name, LinkedIn URL and attachment ids. The number of applicants/attachments is unknown at modeling time, so the problem uses one representative application thread, applicant and attachment: at runtime gmail-show-thread is repeated for every matching thread and gmail-download-attachment for every attachment of every application email, with the target path built from the lower-cased names and the original attachment file name under ~/documents/work/recruiting/attachments/. The CSV is created once after all threads are read (its content aggregates all applicants that provided a LinkedIn URL); file_system creates missing parent directories implicitly, so no create_directory call is modeled. show_thread/download_attachment carry extra non-API parameters (query, applicant) only to link knowledge preconditions. supervisor-complete-task takes the created records as parameters so its precondition equals the task goal and it must be last; no answer is passed since the task asks no question.
